sources.title: Power variation for a class of stationary increments Lévy driven moving averages
sources.locations: 1506.06679 model p2; (A), Theorem1.1(i) pp3–4; Remark2.3 pp9–10. 1603.07382 model p2 and Remark2.2.
sources.read_level: Full primary preprints obtained; controlling statements, remarks and relevant proof structure inspected. Final publisher text retrieval failed.
sources.facts: The model uses a symmetric two-sided Lévy driver. The marked-jump regime requires β<2, p>β and α<k−1/p. A remark describes symmetry as simplifying assumptions and expects most results to persist without it, but omits exact nonsymmetric exposition. Kernel assumptions include an eventually decreasing absolute derivative.
sources.coverage: Known overlap; explicit β restriction excludes index two. Informal symmetry remark is not treated as a separate exact theorem.

sources.title: On limit theory for Lévy semi-stationary processes
sources.read_level: Full primary v2 obtained; model, exact theorem, integrability conditions, topology and marked-regime proof inspected.
sources.facts: The driver is σ_-dL with L symmetric pure-jump Lévy relative to the given filtration and σ adapted càdlàg; independence is not required. Under (A),(B1), β<2, p>β, α<k−1/p, Theorem1.2(i) gives functional stable M1 convergence to weighted jump powers. J1/J2 failure is explicitly discussed.
sources.coverage: Substantial non-Lévy and dependent-volatility prior overlap; no stated arbitrary compensator shape or β=2 conclusion.

sources.title: On limit theory for functionals of stationary increments Lévy driven moving averages
sources.date_caution: NR says July23; Aarhus says September; Crossref has a year-start placeholder. No exact final publication day asserted.
sources.locations: Model(1.1) p2; (A) p4; Theorem2.1(i) p5; Proposition2.3(i)/(FC) p7; proof§4.1–4.4.
sources.read_level: Full primary preprint obtained twice independently; controlling statements and relevant proof inspected. Final publisher PDF retrieval failed.
sources.facts: The model is two-sided Lévy without Gaussian component, with no symmetry restriction. Theorem2.1(i) assumes β<2 and a statistic in C^r with derivatives through floor(r) vanishing at zero, r>max{β,1/(k−α)}. Proposition2.3 supplies finite-dimensional stable convergence and M1 under a sign condition.
sources.coverage: Exact nonsymmetric quadratic overlap via DEDUCTIONS§1. The precisely dated primary preprint controls this finding; no final-version equivalence is assumed.

sources.title: Power variations for fractional type infinitely divisible random fields
sources.read_level: Full primary v3 obtained; model, activity/tail hypotheses and main theorem scopes inspected. Repository publisher postprint request-restricted; no request made.
sources.facts: Noise has independent increments and a deterministic homogeneous symmetric Lévy characteristic measure. Condition (β) imposes 0≤β<2 plus small-jump tail regularity. Condition (θ) separately permits θ=2 when the second jump moment is finite. The statistic uses rectangular increments of deterministic-kernel random fields.
sources.coverage: θ=2 does not remove β<2; no arbitrary predictable jump kernel conclusion.

sources.title: On critical cases in limit theory for stationary increments Lévy driven moving averages
sources.locations: Theorem1.2 and preceding critical-case list pp4–5; quadratic-case discussion.
sources.read_level: Full primary working paper obtained; exact theorem and critical-case discussion inspected.
sources.facts: The new boundaries are α=k−1/p, p>β, and α=k−1/β, p<β/2; the main theorem retains β<2. The p=β boundary remains outside the preceding theorem. The new kernel-boundary limits involve logarithmic normalizations.
sources.coverage: Not an index-two quadratic endpoint theorem.

sources.title: A limit theorem for a class of stationary increments Lévy moving average process with multiple singularities
sources.read_level: Full published primary original obtained; controlling statements inspected.
sources.facts: The model uses a symmetric two-sided Lévy process without Gaussian component. The extension allows multiple kernel singularities; its marked-jump regime retains power above activity. It does not replace the scalar Lévy noise with arbitrary predictable compensator kernels.
sources.coverage: Different kernel geometry, no match to remaining driver scope.

sources.title: Gaussian and non-Gaussian processes of zero power variation
sources.read_level: Full published original obtained; model and non-Gaussian main theorem inspected.
sources.facts: The published model uses a square-integrable continuous martingale. Its non-Gaussian main result concerns vanishing odd-power variation of Volterra integrals and conditions on the derivative of martingale quadratic variation.
sources.coverage: Does not state the normalized jump-square marked stable theorem. Old snippets saying merely martingale are insufficient.

sources.title: A law of large numbers for the power variation of fractional Lévy processes
sources.read_level: Full primary working paper obtained; local-similarity assumptions and both main theorems inspected.
sources.facts: The setting is integrated fractional Lévy processes with local stable behavior, stable index below two, and powers below that index. Its limit is an integrated-volatility law of large numbers proved using local self-similarity and blocking.

sources.facts: The further-reading section cites the 2017 Lévy and 2018 semistationary papers and discusses newer multivariate and infinite-dimensional directions.

sources.title: Shot-noise processes with logarithmic response function and their scaling limits
sources.read_level: Full primary v2 obtained; model, variation discussion and principal scaling theorems inspected.
sources.facts: The response uses a logarithm of the current/event-time ratio. Principal weak convergence scales Poisson shot noise toward a Hadamard fractional Brownian process under changing noise intensity and scale.
sources.coverage: Different response and asymptotic experiment; examined statements do not supply remaining candidate theorem.
